extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party requesters, patent owners, and examiners preparing or evaluating ex parte reexamination requests under 35 U.S.C. 302
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing requests for ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302 / 37 CFR 1.510, including required elements, fees, how to present prior art, and standards for a 'substantial new question of patentability.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of required fee (37 CFR 1.510(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.510(a) requires the payment of the fee specified in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) for a request for reexamination filed under 35 U.S.C. 302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire filing fee must be paid for acceptance, filing date, and Official Gazette publication. If the patent owner files a request that includes a proposed amendment under 37 CFR 1.530, excess claims fees under 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply. Different fees apply for large, small, and micro entities; a requester must affirmatively state small/micro entity status. Only a patent owner can establish micro entity status; third-party requesters cannot. If the fee is missing, the requester will be notified and generally given an opportunity to complete the request; failure to comply will result in no filing date and placement of the request in the patent file as a citation if it otherwise complies with 1.501. Refund rules (37 CFR 1.26) apply if request later denied or vacated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability (37 CFR 1.510(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must include “a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should clearly set forth what the requester considers to be the substantial new question(s) of patentability that warrant reexamination. For each identified SNQ the request must explain how the cited documents raise that SNQ. A requester must not argue in the request that the submitted references do not raise an SNQ (i.e., don't argue that no order should be issued). The determination focuses only on patents and printed publications as sources of SNQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of every claim and detailed explanation applying prior art (37 CFR 1.510(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must include “an identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested, and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must explain, limitation-by-limitation, how each cited reference is applied to each identified claim. If relying on statements submitted under 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2), the request must explain how those statements are being used to determine claim meaning. Patent owner claim scope statements discussed in the detailed explanation are considered at the examination stage but not at the order stage. Preferably provide a detailed claim chart comparing each claim limitation to the relevant teachings of each reference. For proposed obviousness rejections, provide at least one basis for combining references and state why the claim would have been obvious over the combination. Quote pertinent teachings with page/column/line and figure numbers where possible. Avoid lumping claims or combinations together without separate explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of every patent or printed publication relied upon (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to in the request, accompanied by English translations of necessary pertinent parts of any non-English documents, must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies must be legible; if not legible (or not scan-friendly) they are deemed not provided and will be identified in a Notice of Failure to Comply. Color photos retained as artifact files if legible. A mere abstract or summary of a non-English document is usually insufficient; translate necessary parts. The requirement to submit copies is waived for U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications to the extent permitted by 37 CFR 1.98, unless specifically required by the Office. Do not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings/applications; provide application/proceeding numbers and status instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the entire patent for which reexamination is requested (37 CFR 1.510(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the entire patent including the front face, drawings, and specification/claims (in double column format where the patent is printed) must be supplied, together with any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent. All copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full copy of the printed patent (including front page) can be used to provide abstract, drawings, specification, and claims. The printed patent should be reproduced on only one side of paper; two-sided copies are improper. Copies of any disclaimers or correction certificates are required so the complete patent is supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service on patent owner for third-party requests (37 CFR 1.510(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in § 1.33(c), indicating the name and address of the party served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible after reasonable effort, supply a duplicate copy to the Office with a cover letter explaining efforts and why service failed. To avoid erroneous duplicate filing fees, include a clearly worded cover letter (e.g., bold heading: “Duplicate Copy... When Service on the Patent Owner Was Not Possible”). If the requester is a third party, this certification is mandatory; failure to provide it will render the request defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel certification for third-party requesters (37 CFR 1.510(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification by the third-party requester that the statutory estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 35 U.S.C. 325(e)(1) do not prohibit the requester from filing the ex parte reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that a petitioner (or real party in interest/privy) in inter partes review or post-grant review is not estopped from seeking ex parte reexamination. Rules do not require requesters to identify themselves on filing; an anonymous real party may use a registered practitioner who certifies the real party is not estopped. An individual filing on his/her own behalf cannot remain anonymous because signature is required on the certification. The 11.18 practitioner's certification obligations apply when transacting business before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness for filing date and consequences of incompleteness (37 CFR 1.510(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not include the fee and meet all requirements of 37 CFR 1.510(b), the person identified as requesting reexamination will generally be notified and given opportunity to complete the request; failure to comply results in no filing date. The filing date is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete requests that are not cured may be placed in the patent file as a citation under 37 CFR 1.501 if they otherwise comply with that rule. Notices of Failure to Comply will identify defects and allow either cure or opportunity to withdraw particular documents/claims/combinations. Refunds may apply if request later denied or vacated per 37 CFR 1.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability standard (35 U.S.C. 304 / MPEP § 2216)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 304 the Office must determine whether “a substantial new question of patentability” affecting any claim of the patent has been raised. The request must demonstrate an SNQ based on patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not sufficient merely to propose rejections; the cited patent or publication must present a new, non-cumulative technological teaching that was not previously considered and discussed during prosecution or prior proceedings. Old art may raise an SNQ only if presented/viewed in a new light or different way with a material new argument or interpretation (e.g., new analysis under KSR rationales). KSR did not alter the SNQ legal standard. Questions based on matters other than patents/printed publications (public use, on sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101/112, conduct) should not be included and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of old art in a new light
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents and printed publications previously cited or considered by the Office (“old art”) may raise a substantial new question of patentability only if the old art is presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way compared with its prior use in earlier examination(s) in view of a material new argument or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request that simply asks the Office to re-evaluate previously-considered art solely on the basis of changes in the legal standard (e.g., KSR) without presenting the art in a new way will not raise an SNQ. The request should articulate the material new analysis that makes the old art newly pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation must be complete and specific (I. EXPLANATION MUST BE COMPLETE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere citation of patents or printed publications without an explanation does not comply with 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2). The requester must present an explanation of how the cited documents are applied to all claims which the requester considers to merit reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include citations to background references not used to support an SNQ or proposed rejection. For each proposed combination, explain how each reference is used and applied to each claim (e.g., claims 1-10: explain application to claim 1, claim 2, etc.). Preferred format is a detailed claim chart. For obviousness proposals, provide at least one basis to combine references and explain why the claim would have been obvious over the combination. Avoid language that lumps alternative references or combinations together; the MPEP provides specific 'inappropriate' and 'appropriate' language examples. If a Notice of Failure to Comply identifies missing explanations, the requester may either (A) provide separate explanations for each identified combination/document/claim, or (B) explicitly withdraw any document/combination/claim lacking explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of inappropriate vs appropriate claim-language and combination statements
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP gives explicit examples of inappropriate language (e.g., lumping alternatives or multiple combinations together) and appropriate language (e.g., specifying claim-by-claim rejections and explicit combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, claim-specific rejection statements such as 'Claim 1 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Smith in view of Jones.' Avoid alternatives like 'Smith and/or Charles' or grouping claims and many alternative combinations in a single sentence unless each alternative is separately articulated and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Notices of Failure to Comply
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request lacks required explanations for documents/combinations/claims, the Office will issue a 'Notice of Failure to Comply with Ex Parte Reexamination Request Filing Requirements' identifying the defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester may respond by supplying separate explanations for each identified defect or by explicitly withdrawing the defective document/combination/claim from the request. Withdrawing reduces what need be explained; e.g., withdrawing claims 6-10 means only claims 1-5 require application of the documents/combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits, declarations, and other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evidence may assist in clarifying dates or contents of cited references; see MPEP § 2258 for further treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions — scope and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration under 35 U.S.C. 303 is limited to prior art patents and printed publications; an admission per se may not be the basis for establishing an SNQ, but admissions may be utilized in combination with patents/printed publications to determine scope and content of prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions in the patent file or court record may be used by the examiner in combination with patents/printed publications. A third party may not submit out-of-record admissions of the patent owner unless they are entered into a court record and filed as a copy of a paper filed in the court; even then such submissions are outside the normal scope of reexamination and would not carry weight as admissions establishing an SNQ. Admissions must stand on their own; supplemental information to define the admission is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility and format requirements for submitted copies (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3) / §2218)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted copies of patents/printed publications must be legible and scan appropriately for the Image File Wrapper (IFW) system; non-legible documents are deemed not provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color photographs/like color submissions, if legible, will be retained as artifacts. For non-English documents, provide English translations of all necessary and pertinent parts; abstracts or summaries are usually insufficient. The Office may waive providing copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent publications per 37 CFR 1.98 unless specifically required. Do not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings or applications; supply application/proceeding numbers and status instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on claim types of questions presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions of patentability in reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302 must be based on patents or printed publications; other matters (public use, on sale, conduct, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, 35 U.S.C. 112, etc.) will not be considered in determining whether to order reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior art patent or printed publication cannot be used merely to evidence alleged public use or on sale or insufficiency of disclosure; it must be applied directly to claims under 35 U.S.C. 103 and/or appropriate portions of 35 U.S.C. 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form PTO/SB/57 and transmittal guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/57 should be helpful to persons filing requests for reexamination under 37 CFR 1.510; its use as the transmittal form and cover sheet is encouraged but not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of PTO/SB/57 can help ensure the request meets formal transmittal expectations. The MPEP includes a sample PTO/SB/57 and a sample request that can be attached to the form cover sheet. An application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 generally cannot be submitted in a reexamination proceeding except as provided in MPEP § 2258.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity via registered practitioner and signing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules do not require ex parte reexamination requesters to identify themselves on filing; anonymous real parties in interest may utilize a registered practitioner to file the request on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered practitioner submitting on behalf of a real party would certify that the real party is not estopped under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(6). An individual filing on his/her own behalf cannot remain anonymous because the individual must sign the certification including the estoppel statement.
